task.title: Page pending due one-shot schedules sparsely through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/1003 by exposing bounded pending-due schedule scans as deterministic read-only JSON.
acceptance_criteria: Parse the explicit cutoff and validate a positive at-most-1024 scan size plus optional exact schedule-ID cursor before storage access.
Emit complete pending-due schedules in exact-ID scan order with the kernel-owned nullable last-inspected continuation cursor.
Preserve missing-storage non-creation and fail without partial stdout on selected-window corruption or serialization failure.

attempts.diagnostic: The CLI rejected schedule due-page because the subcommand did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added tests for sparse mixed lifecycle and due pages, inclusive cutoff, ordering, escaping, validation, missing storage, and corruption boundaries.

attempts.summary: Implemented and refactored the read-only adapter.
attempts.diagnostic: Implemented pre-storage size and cursor validation, read-only list_due_page delegation, and compact JSON using the canonical complete schedule projection.
attempts.patch: Implemented issue 1003 in crates/vela-dev/src/lib.rs with CLI tests, ADR-0100, and scheduler documentation; independent review found no blocking issue.

attempts.diagnostic: A review-limit false green was excluded; after cooldown and shared-budget recheck, CodeRabbit command 28c5e937 completed on exact head d923e01 with no actionable comments and zero unresolved threads.
attempts.patch: Kept auto-merge disabled until exact-head Rust CI and the deliberate genuine review succeeded.

outcome.summary: Issue 1003 exposed bounded pending-due schedule paging without changing complete due discovery or granting mutation authority.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate for pull request 1004 exact head d923e01a6a64b3f26a0a249786c438f72783b8b2

lessons: An explicit due-page command avoids silently changing complete schedule due ordering and output compatibility.
Sparse pages can contain no schedules while next_after still proves bounded scan progress.
The CLI serializes kernel continuation directly and adds no dense-fill scan, ambient clock, persisted cursor, lifecycle, dispatch, permission, or execution authority.
